messages:
maya: FYI ran a few internal load-test variants this morning against staging rate limiter. Observed 429 spikes when we inject bursts > 300 req/s for a single API key; tail latency also jumped. Quick summary below.

josh: Can you paste the exact harness/command? Is this per-worker or aggregated?

maya: command: ```./loadtest --endpoint https://staging.api.redwood.ai/generate --keys 50 --rps 1000 --burst 800 --duration 600``` (we run across 5 workers). note: keys recycled per worker. We saw quota_exhausted errors: "Quota exceeded for customer" (429). Logs show token_bucket refills at 1s granularity.

liu: Important — our current default is RPM=6000 and burst=1200 per project (legacy). That explains it. Did you test with token-size/avg tokens param? Larger outputs use more token budget than request-count limits suggest.

maya: avg response ~220 tokens. So token accounting is the blocker: 1 req ~= 220 tokens, so TPM drained much faster than RPM.

avery: We should test both request-based and token-based limits. Proposed matrix: RPM per-key {200,1200,6000}, TPM per-key {5k,20k,60k}, burst multipliers {2x,5x}. Sweep combinations.

helen: Capture p50/p95/p99 latency, 429 rate, and error categories (auth vs quota vs rate). Use this quick observability query and tweak timeframe:
```sql
select error_type, count(*) as cnt, percentile(latency_ms, 95) as p95
from requests
where env='staging' and ts >= '2025-10-01'
group by error_type;
```

maya: repro steps I'm saving for support playbook:
1) spin up 6 workers on m5.xlarge
2) each holds 10 API keys
3) 10m linear ramp to target rps, hold 5m, then cool down
4) record metrics: requests, tokens, 429s, retry-after, queue-time, p99
I will push artifacts to /tmp/loadtest-run-1762001123.tgz

infra-bot: scheduled job "burst-sweep-1762001123" created, running on k8s job ci-loadtests us-west-2, ETA 15m.

josh: What is our current queue policy when token bucket empty? Fast-fail or short queue? I recall we queue up to 50ms then return 429.

liu: Queueing had big impact: p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~450ms in the runs where queueing was enabled. My preference: fast-fail to protect latency SLOs, expose Retry-After and recommend client backoff.

maya: Agreed — for production defaults we should lean fast-fail. For Dedicated/enterprise tiers we can expose longer queue windows.

avery: For default sane defaults I propose: RPM=1200, TPM=30000 (tokens/min), burst capacity = 3x per-second replenish (i.e., token_bucket_size = 3 * rate_per_sec). Also soft per-key concurrency cap = 50. This keeps 429s low for spiky traffic while limiting cost impact.

helen: Sounds reasonable as a baseline. Note: customers with long responses (avg tokens >500) will hit TPM first. Add guidance in docs to convert tokens->requests for typical payload sizes.

josh: I'll run a full sweep and produce a CSV: columns = run_id, rps_target, tokens_per_min, burst_multiplier, 429_rate, p99_latency_ms. Will link the artifact. Also opening a GH issue to track PR to docs.

maya: tagging @support to update the escalation playbook with repro steps and quick checks: check project quota in console, run curl to reproduce, collect /metrics/rate_limiter, include client key and peak concurrency, and attach loadtest artifacts.

support-bot: ticket RDW-5122 created linking this thread (priority: medium).

maya: run finished (summary): best default for general workloads: RPM=1200, TPM=30000, burst_capacity=3600 (3x/sec). At target load 1.2k RPM we saw 429s <0.1% and p99 ~230ms. Pushing a short PR to update docs and playbook, will drop CSV and plots into the GH issue.

helen: awesome — please include the exact harness command and env vars in the PR so support can repro locally.

josh: noted, I'll attach the CSV and the k8s job spec.

maya: thanks y'all. If customers hit quota issues we can point to this thread + the repro steps. I'll follow up in ~30m with links to artifacts.
